summary: Adds new eval fixtures and definitions for the debug-loop skill. evals.json defines five evals (ids 0-4: vague-login-failure, pasted-traceback, red-tests-after-merge, trivial-typo-fast-path, perf-regression-threshold-check), each with a prompt and a list of expectations the skill's output must satisfy. Also adds the csv-report fixture: a report.py script that reads a CSV and sums amounts by region, a sales CSV with a UTF-8 BOM prefix on its header line, clean and header-only test CSVs, and a test_report.py with two tests (normal totals, empty file).

claims.text: evals.json defines 5 evals for skill "debug-loop" with ids 0 through 4
Eval 1 (pasted-traceback) expects the skill to identify a UTF-8 BOM in the export header as the cause of the KeyError
report.total_by_region reads a CSV with csv.DictReader and sums amount by region key
The fixture CSV sales-2026-08.csv has a BOM character before "region" in its header row
load() opens the file with encoding="utf-8" (not utf-8-sig), so a BOM would remain attached to the first header field
test_report.py's two tests use clean.csv and header_only.csv, neither of which contains a BOM
Running report.py against sales-2026-08.csv raises KeyError: 'region' while the checked-in test suite stays green

risks.note: No test in this fixture covers a BOM-prefixed CSV; the only file exhibiting the bug (sales-2026-08.csv) is used solely as the eval prompt's repro data, not as a test case, so the existing suite cannot catch the bug the eval is designed around.
Both files hold identical region/amount rows (east 10.0, west 12.5, east 20.0); the only difference is the BOM, which is easy to miss when comparing the two.

least_confident: I could not directly confirm the BOM byte sequence in sales-2026-08.csv beyond the visual ﻿ marker shown before "region" in the diff text, since I cannot run code or inspect raw bytes.
